name: Cu Chi food
summary: Eat on a tunnel day. Rice paper from Phú Hòa Đông, cassava, Cu Chi veal, pork-knuckle noodle soup, and durian sugarcane juice on National Highway 22 are the plates with a published account. A long meal is in Ho Chi Minh City.
body: Boiled cassava at the Hoàng Cầm kitchen comes with sesame salt and hot tea. Tuổi Trẻ, on 5 May 2024, dips the same root in salt. Both stay. The Ho Chi Minh City Tourism Promotion Center also places Cu Chi veal, pork-knuckle noodle soup, durian sugarcane juice along National Highway 22, and rambutan, mangosteen, durian, and jackfruit at Trung An.

Phú Hòa Đông rice paper is dried in the sun. One mix is rice flour with coconut water, salt, sugar, and sesame depending on the batch. An older mix is rice flour, water, and salt. The craft is more than 50 years in Báo Quốc tế and more than 80 years in Tạp chí Công Thương. The gazette decision gives no start year.
Veal in rice paper is boiled on two accounts and grilled just done on the third. Steamed cassava is pandan or coconut cream on one account, and both together on another.
specialtiesLead: Rice paper, cassava, Cu Chi veal, pork-knuckle noodle soup, and durian sugarcane juice, then the other plates with a published account.

sections.heading: More plates
paragraphs: These are the other plates recorded for Củ Chi.

spots.name: Cassava rolled in rice paper
spots.nameVi: khoai mì quết cuốn bánh tráng
spots.note: Cassava boiled in coconut water, mashed with sugar, salt, and scallion oil, then rolled in rice paper with herbs and pork or shrimp. The dip is garlic fish sauce, with chili in one wording.

spots.name: Cassava bánh tằm
spots.note: Bánh tằm made from Củ Chi cassava flour.

spots.name: Veal rolled in rice paper
spots.note: Thin veal rolled in rice paper with forest greens, boiled until soft and fragrant, or soft and sweet with crisp skin. One account grills the meat just done and rolls it the same way.

spots.name: Crispy rice with kho veal
spots.note: Kho veal eaten with crispy rice. One wording is cơm cháy bò tơ kho, and another is lemongrass kho veal with the same crisp rice.

spots.name: Durian sugarcane juice
spots.note: Sugarcane juice along National Highway 22, cool, with the aroma of durian. One account uses mung bean in place of the fruit.

spots.name: Bamboo-shoot salad
spots.note: Bamboo shoot shaved and boiled, then mixed with belly pork, shrimp, rau răm, fried shallot, and peanuts. Sweet-sour fish sauce is tossed in, or left on the side.

spots.name: Young jackfruit salad
spots.note: Boiled young jackfruit mixed with pork and shrimp, sweet-sour fish sauce, herbs, and sesame. One account also adds chicken.

spots.name: Frog with lá lốt
spots.note: Frog stir-fried with the skin on, finished with young lá lốt.

spots.name: Grilled arowana
spots.nameVi: cá hải tượng nướng muối ớt
spots.note: Arowana grilled with salt and chili. One account seasons it with satay over charcoal and serves green-chili salt and herbs.

spots.name: Chicken grilled in a clay pot
spots.note: Chicken grilled in a clay pot over embers, with crisp golden skin and meat that stays soft. It comes with crispy rice, scallion fat, and lemongrass salt.

spots.name: Beef hoof and tendon porridge
spots.note: Porridge of beef hoof and tendon with mung beans, peanuts, white beans, and cassava, finished with rau má and leafy greens.

spots.name: Giant freshwater prawn
spots.address: Kênh Đông and the Sài Gòn river
spots.note: Giant freshwater prawn from kênh Đông and the Sài Gòn river, with meat that is fresh, sweet, and firm. It is grilled, steamed, or cooked in a hotpot.

spots.name: Pickled rau móp
spots.note: Pickled rau móp, sour, crisp, and cool, made from the young leaves and tips.

spots.name: Eel and taro porridge
spots.note: Eel and taro porridge with lemongrass and mắm ruốc. The eel is sweet and the taro is soft.

spots.name: Crisp-fried cá trèn
spots.note: Cá trèn fried until the skin is crisp.

spots.name: Loofah stir-fried with lá quế
spots.note: Loofah stir-fried with lá quế.

spots.name: Grilled sparrow
spots.note: Sparrow grilled over a fire.

spots.name: Chim lá
spots.note: Chim lá, one of the countryside dishes.

spots.name: Stir-fried bánh lọt
spots.address: chợ Củ Chi and chợ Việt Kiều
spots.note: Stir-fried bánh lọt from chợ Củ Chi and chợ Việt Kiều.

spots.name: Veal dipped in vinegar
spots.note: Veal cooked by dipping it in vinegar.

spots.name: Veal dipped in hèm
spots.note: Veal dipped in hèm.

spots.name: Beef porridge
spots.note: Beef porridge, a separate bowl from the hoof-and-tendon porridge.

spots.name: Chả đùm veal
spots.note: Chả đùm made with veal.

spots.name: Oxtail hotpot
spots.note: Oxtail hotpot.

spots.name: Beef offal steamed with ginger
spots.note: Beef offal steamed with ginger.

spots.name: Turmeric stir-fried veal
spots.note: Veal stir-fried with turmeric.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: Two workshop lanes and two town markets.

spots.name: Phú Hòa Đông rice-paper lanes
spots.nameVi: làng nghề bánh tráng Phú Hòa Đông
spots.address: xã Phú Hòa Đông, on the river
spots.note: Workshop lanes in xã Phú Hòa Đông, where rice-paper sheets dry on racks. Walk them on a tunnel outing.

spots.name: Chợ Quê
spots.note: The market inside the tunnel gate, where visitors eat on the 2021 reopening. The gate that day runs 7:00–17:00.

spots.name: Chợ Củ Chi
spots.note: A town market for steamed cassava, stir-fried bánh lọt, bánh bao, hủ tiếu, chicken bánh canh, and Cambodian-style bánh khọt.

spots.name: Chợ Việt Kiều
spots.note: The other market for those same plates, paired with chợ Củ Chi.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Pork-knuckle noodle soup is the local breakfast.

spots.name: Pork knuckle noodle soup
spots.note: Pork-knuckle noodle soup, the long-standing local breakfast.
